title: Core starter kit
description: What packages/core contains, what gets copied into a new template, and when to use optional sync.

blocks.text: packages/core is not a runtime dependency. It is a generic boilerplate copied once when you run pnpm new-template. After that, the template folder is a complete Next.js app — all imports resolve locally with @/.

blocks.title: No template names in core
blocks.text: Core must stay vertical-agnostic: no hotel pages, no real-estate models, no client brand copy. Only reusable auth, leads, storage, health, and shared UI pieces.

rows: Minimal app/layout.tsx, app/page.tsx, GETTING_STARTED.md from packages/core/scaffold/

blocks.text: What is NOT copied / you add yourself

items: Home page, Hero, Footer, domain listing grids
Models in prisma/domain.prisma (hotel: RoomType; real-estate: Project)
Template-specific seeds, scripts, and public assets

blocks.code:
pnpm new-template bakery bakery-website-template --name "Bakery Website"
# Copies packages/core + scaffold → templates/bakery-website-template/
# Updates templates.json, adds pnpm dev:bakery, merges prisma/schema.prisma

blocks.text: If you fix a bug in packages/core and want existing templates to receive it without hand-copying files:
Normal template development does not use sync. Use pnpm template:diff-core before propagate to see what would change.

First slice implemented: enquiry-modal, footer, hero-simple via pnpm new-template --modules and pnpm template:add-module. Next: gallery, reviews, leadrat, seo, and tempjs add-module for client projects.
